prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone in St. Louis — the right contractor depends on your budget, the size and scope of the job, desired finish and timeline, and whether you want extras (color consulting, trim/cabinet work, repairs). I can help you find the best match. Here’s a quick, practical way to identify top interior painters in St. Louis and vet them.

How to find strong candidates
- Search reviews on Google, Yelp and the Better Business Bureau (BBB) for contractors in your zip code. Look for consistently high ratings and recent reviews.
- Ask neighbors, friends, or local Facebook/Nextdoor groups for recommendations and before/after photos.
- Look at each company’s portfolio on their website or social media to confirm they do work like yours (historical homes, smooth modern finishes, etc.).
- Verify license/insurance and ask for proof of general liability and workers’ comp.

Questions to ask every painter
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?
- Do you provide a written estimate and contract? What’s included (prep, repairs, number of coats, type of paint)?
- Which paint brands and finishes do you use? Do you offer low-VOC options?
- What surface prep will you do (patching, sanding, priming)?
- How many people will work on my job and what is the expected timeline?
- Do you provide a warranty or touch-up guarantee?
- Can you provide recent references I can contact?

Red flags to avoid
- Very low bids that come without a written scope.
- No proof of insurance or license.
- Poor communication or refusal to provide references.
- Demand for large upfront payment (30% or less is typical; never full payment up front).

Typical cost ranges (ballpark)
- Per room (standard bedroom): $300–$1,000 depending on size, prep and trim.
- Per square foot: commonly $1.50–$4.00 for walls/ceilings; higher with heavy repairs or high-end finishes.
(Prices vary by scope and materials; get at least 3 written bids.)

If you want, I can:
- Suggest specific highly-reviewed St. Louis companies if you want me to research (you’ll need to provide names or allow me to look things up — I can’t browse the web in this chat unless you paste links/info).
- Vet a short list you’ve found (I’ll tell you what to look for in their estimates and references).
- Help draft a checklist or contract items to include for your job.

Tell me the job size (number of rooms, any repairs, trim/cabinets) or paste 3 company names you’re considering and I’ll help compare them.
